subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should unset Docker sandbox `pidsLimit` become a 1024-process cap by default, and what explicit opt-out value should preserve Docker default/unlimited behavior?
rationale: This is a sandbox security boundary and upgrade-compatibility choice; the code can implement it, but automation should not choose the default value or accepted opt-out semantics for existing deployments.

options.title: Approve capped default with opt-out
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep the 1024 default only after aligning schema, type docs, user docs, tests, and real Docker proof for an explicit unlimited/Docker-default escape hatch.

options.title: Keep current default
options.body: Leave unset `pidsLimit` as Docker default/unlimited and redirect this to stronger docs or operator hardening guidance.

options.title: Choose a different cap or mode
options.body: Pick a different default value or opt-in strict mode, then request a narrow implementation that proves fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve capped default with opt-out
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep the 1024 default only after aligning schema, type docs, user docs, tests, and real Docker proof for an explicit unlimited/Docker-default escape hatch.
